8 Driving in fog
Fog is very dangerous as, not only does it reduce visibility but the adhesion quality (grip) is also lowered, as the road surface becomes wet.
Therefore, when driving in fog it is necessary to:
Use lights: the front dipped headlights or / and the front fog light (if fitted) together with the position lights and, in the case of thick fog, the rear fog light(s).
It is not recommended to use the main beam headlights as the fog reflects back the vehicles own lights (the water drops act like a mirror) and cases dazzle to the driver.
Keep the cabin well ventilated to avoid the windows misting up.
Adapt the speed to the visibility and view of the road ahead.
 
(Página 232 del manual 'Learning to drive')

6. Groups of drivers most at risk of a collision
6.1 The young
6.1.1 The primary cause of juvenile mortality 
Young drivers generally have a number of advantages over the remainder of drivers, as generally they are in a better condition of physical fitness, have better reflexes and skills that are more suited to driving. However, these favourable conditions do not help if the driver is not aware of his limitations, including lack of experience or the tendency to take more risks.
There are many young people who drive safely and therefore have no increased risk of being involved in a collision than other older drivers.
However, in Spain each year hundreds of young people die in road traffic collisions, which are the leading cause of death in the 15 to 29 year age group. Therefore the problem of road collisions is even more worrying for young people in this age group than for others outside it.
 
(Página 253 del manual 'Learning to drive')

17 Influence of drugs in road traffic collisions
The consumption of illegal drugs is related to many of the most serious accidents. A person driving under the influence of drugs puts all those around him/her at serious risk of accidents.

It is forbidden to drive any vehicle with presence of drugs in the body. Maneouvres      
     
5 Overtaking  
5.3 Manoeuvres that are not considered overtakes
5.3.2 Special lanes
It is not considered to be overtaking, when a vehicle travels faster in either an acceleration lane – in order to enter a road; or on a deceleration lane - in order to exit a road and in doing so, passes vehicles. Additionally, this is also the case, in a lane that is marked for a specific route and direction or, a lane for certain predetermined vehicles.
However it is considered to be an overtake, when a vehicle enters into an acceleration or deceleration lane purely in order to pass another vehicle or enters into special lane, whose function is to facilitate slower moving traffic.
(Página 187 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.5 Safety distance
Any driver of a vehicle driving behind another must leave space that allows them to stop without colliding in the event of sudden braking, taking into account, in particular, speed, grip and braking conditions. However, a group of cyclists does not need to keep this distance, paying close attention to avoid collisions.
When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. (Note: that his rule is not applicable to a group of cyclists travelling together.)
Vehicles with a MAM greater than 3500 kgs, vehicles and combinations / sets of vehicles over 10m long, must keep a minimum safety distance of 50 m.
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Generic speed            
           
5.1 Maximum speed limits on interurban roads           
5.1.2 Conventional roads   
Motor vehicles must not exceed the following speed limits:
- Passenger cars, motorbikes, three-wheeled vehicles similar to motorbikes, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass ≤ 3,500 kg and pick-up trucks: 90 km/h.(1)
- Buses, passenger car derivatives and mixed adaptable vehicles: 90 km/h.
- Lorries, trailers, vans, camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass > 3,500 kg, articulated vehicles, cars with a trailer and all other vehicles: 80 km/h.  
- Motor tricycles not assimilated to motorcycles and heavy quadricycle: 70 km/h.
(1) On conventional roads with physical separation of the two directions of traffic movement, the road owner may set a speed limit of 100 km/h for passenger cars, motorbikes and camper vans with a Maximum Authorised Mass equal to or less than 3,500 kg.
(Página 173 del manual 'Learning to drive')

questions.help:
3 Use of lanes    
   
3.2 Lanes within built-up-areas
The drivers of automobiles and special vehicles (regardless of their weight) may use the most appropriate lane for their direction of travel that is best suited to their destination and intended route. As long as these lanes are defined by longitudinal lines and appropriately indicated and drivers do not cause inconvenience to other road users. This rule will not be applicable on motorways or dual carriageways within city limits.
(Página 162 del manual 'Learning to drive')
